summary: Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Ernst Kuhn. He worked at the University of Munich from 1893 to 1916 and headed the Museum Fünf Kontinente starting in 1907.

Luciano Petech worked in Tibetology and history and archaeology after studying under Giuseppe Tucci. He served as Lector at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at the University of Rome (1955–1984).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl worked in philosophy and religious studies, having studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He later served on the faculty at the University of Paris from circa 1899 to 1927.

Linguist Lucien Tesnière studied at the Universities of Paris and Leipzig, the École des Langues Orientales, and under Antoine Meillet. He held appointments at the Universities of Strasbourg and Ljubljana (1924–1937) and the University of Montpellier (1937).

Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under doctoral supervisors Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, and also studied under Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Ghent University and SOAS, training under Adriaan Scharpé, Jan Gonda, and others. He served as professor at the Free University of Brussels (1959–1966) and chair at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2002).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Walther Schubring, Heinrich Lüders, Heinrich Zimmer, and Christian Bartholomae. He taught at Allahabad, Berlin, Münster, and held the Indian history and culture chair at Hamburg (1950–1972).

Ludwig Diestel was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at the University of Bonn (~1851–1862), Greifswald (~1862–1867), Jena (~1867–1872), and Tübingen (~1872–1879).

Ludwig Heller was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Kielhorn at the University of Göttingen and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He served as an extraordinary professor at Greifswald (1904) and held a post at Tartu (1918).

Ludwig Lange was a scholar in philosophy who studied at the Universities of Leipzig and Göttingen, studying under Theodor Benfey. He held academic posts at Göttingen, Prague, Giessen (~1859–1871), and Leipzig (~1871–1885).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at the Technische Hochschule Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge. He later served as a lecturer, fellow, and professor of philosophy at Cambridge between 1929 and 1947.
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He held an appointment as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.
Luigi Suali was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi. He held an academic post at the University of Pavia from circa 1907 to 1951.

Luis Oscar Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale University under Stanley Insler, and the University of Michigan. He served as department chairman at the University of Michigan.

Luise Hercus was an Indologist and linguist who studied at St Anne's College, Oxford, and the Australian National University. She held posts at St Anne's College, the University of Adelaide, and the Australian National University.
Lungten Dubgyur is a Tibetology scholar with legal expertise who completed studies at Sherubtse College, Government Law College in Mumbai, and the University of Edinburgh.

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and at Kyangtsang Monastery. He was a lecturer at the University of Oslo in 1967 and became abbot of Menri Monastery in 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima was a scholar who pursued studies under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Lutz Bieg is a Sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Heidelberg and his habilitation at the Free University of Berlin. He was a professor of Chinese literature and philosophy at the University of Cologne from 1989 to 2008.
Lynn Struve is a Sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Washington and the University of Michigan. She held a faculty post at Indiana University from circa 1977 to 2011.
